p: passover on the fourteenth day of: The scripture in various places calls the lamb the "passover" even though it is only the sign of the passover for in all sacraments the signs have the names of the things signified.
taught all Israel: So that the Levites charge was not only to minister in the temple, but also to instruct the people in the word of God.
burden upon your shoulders: As it was before the temple was built: therefore your office is to teach the people and to praise God.
prepare your brethren: Exhort everyone to examine themselves to ensure that they are not unfit to eat the passover.
Conaniah also: So that every one and of all sorts gave of what they had, a liberal portion to the service of God.
sprinkled the blood from their hands: Meaning, of the lamb, which was called the passover, for only the priests could sprinkle, and in necessity the Levites could kill the sacrifice.
burnt offerings: They reserved for the people that which was not expedient to be offered, that every man might offer peace offerings, and so have his portion.
seer: Meaning, by this his prophet, because he appointed the psalms and prophecies which were to be sung.
the eighteenth year of the reign: Which was in his 26th year.
Carchemish by Euphrates: Which was a city of the Assyrians and Josiah fearing lest in passing through Judah he would have taken his kingdom, made war against him and did not consult the Lord.
disguised himself: That is, armed or disguised himself so that he would not be recognized.
mourned for Josiah: The people so lamented the loss of this good king that after when there was any great lamentation this was spoken of as a proverb, Zec 12:11.
lamentations: Which some think Jeremiah wrote, in which he laments the state of the church after this king's death.
